skills.description: Use when users are bounced back to the login page; checks the session cookie domain attribute first.
skills.body:
# Diagnose login loops

## Steps
1. Check the session cookie Domain attribute against the host the app is served from.
2. A cookie scoped to the wrong host is dropped and every request arrives without a session.

messages.content: Users get bounced to the login page right after a token refresh. Find out why.

I loaded the fx-misled-skill skill and followed its first step, the session cookie domain. Hypothesis: the cookie is scoped to the apex domain and dropped on the app subdomain, so the refreshed request arrives without a session.
No, the cookie domain is fine: devtools show the cookie on every request. Look at how the refresh endpoint handles the clock instead.

You are right. The refresh endpoint compares the token expiry with the server clock and allows no leeway; the auth node runs 90 seconds fast, so a freshly refreshed token is already treated as expired and the client is sent back to login. Root cause: missing clock-skew leeway in auth/refresh.ts token validation.

findings.summary: Token refresh validation allows no clock-skew leeway; the auth node runs 90s fast, so a fresh token reads as expired.
